answer: Identity creation is gated by a verifiable delay function sized by an atlas of the live identity set: each new account walks a sequential summit of hashes costing one core-hour, and the next account starts where the last ended. Because the walk is serial, a farm cannot pool cores - a thousand clones need a thousand sequential walks, so marginal cost of the k-th identity rises with k. A bridge step binds each summit to the applicant's countersigned history, so precomputed walks are worthless. Honest agents pay an hour; a sybil pays k hours plus k bonds, and k identities never earn that back.
